hypotheses.reasoning: payment-svc charges were healthy (20-90ms) until 12:11:42Z. Then the external card processor (api.cardproc.example) slowed to 5s, then 10s, then hung until the 30s upstream timeout (#147, #156). order-service's PaymentClient calls timed out at 30s (#148, #157). Those hung calls filled the HTTP pool to payment-svc (50/50 in use, #159) and pool checkouts started timing out (#169). That made order-service return 503s, which surface at the gateway as POST /checkout 503 (#163 onward). These are symptoms. No deploys, and postgres, redis and order-consumer logged no warnings or errors. GC and heap look normal.
The third-party card processor is degraded, but it hangs instead of failing fast or reporting itself down, so dependency_timeout fits better.
The payment-svc pool hit 50/50, but only because calls were hanging. The pool is not undersized for normal load.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check the card processor's status and escalate to the vendor. Cut the payment-svc timeout to the processor from 30s to about 5s, and add a circuit breaker so calls fail fast. Also make order-service's timeout to payment-svc shorter than the gateway timeout, and isolate its pool so hung charges can't use up every connection. If a backup processor is available, consider failing over to it or queueing charges.
